convention: literal line-by-line, Latin order kept where English allows, every word rendered, nothing added
reasoning_summary:
2b: Merrill has no separate 2b; it prints lines 11-13 inside poem 2 after a gap line "10a" (". . . . . . . ."), so the gap marker is kept in the English with a note naming the fragment.
10 (Bithynia): the exchange is rendered line by line with quotation marks added only to mark speakers (the Latin has none, noted); irrumator is rendered plainly as "mouth-fucker" with a note, cinaediorem as "rather shameless" with a note on cinaedus; run-together source punctuation (deferri.Mane, mihi?crede in 12) is kept exactly in the Latin field and noted.
11: obscenity kept plain ("the groins bursting", with a note that ilia rumpens means draining them sexually); the word split ulti-/mosque is mirrored as furth-/-est so each English line carries only its own Latin.
6: ecfututa rendered "fucked-out"; line 12 is textually doubtful and is translated as Merrill prints it, with a note.
13: unguentum rendered literally "an unguent" (perfumed ointment), with a note that some take it as the girl's own scent; sale noted as both salt and wit.
Run-over clauses (e.g. 4.6-7 double negative, 4.20-21 utrumque ... in pedem, 2.9 possem as a wish) are split by what stands on each line, with notes where the sense needs the next line; no lines reordered.
